partners.mechanism_chain: GATA1 (HGNC:4119) —DISRUPTS→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001896); ITGA2B (HGNC:6044) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 signaling (REACT:R-HSA-6799071); Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 signaling (REACT:R-HSA-6799071) —DISRUPTS→ Impaired platelet aggregation (HP:0011241); Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001896) —LEADS_TO→ Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 signaling (REACT:R-HSA-6799071); Thrombasthenia (HP:0001927) —LEADS_TO→ Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 signaling (REACT:R-HSA-6799071); Impaired platelet aggregation (HP:0011241) —LEADS_TO→ Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 signaling (REACT:R-HSA-6799071). Mutations in GATA1 (causing X-linked thrombocytopenia) and ITGA2B (causing Glanzmann thrombasthenia) both converge on the disruption of Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 signaling, which is essential for platelet aggregation and overall hemostasis. While GATA1 mutations directly impact megakaryopoiesis and platelet production, leading to thrombocytopenia, ITGA2B mutations directly impair the function of the integrin complex itself, resulting in thrombasthenia and impaired aggregation. Both ultimately lead to a phenotype of abnormal bleeding due to defective platelet function or quantity, converging on the shared pathway of integrin signaling.

partners.mechanism_chain: GATA1 (HGNC:4137) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0030097); Hematopoiesis (GO:0030097) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001874); Hematopoiesis (GO:0030097) —LEADS_TO→ Dyserythropoietic anemia (HP:0001892); H3-3A (HGNC:4855) —DISRUPTS→ Histone modifications (GO:0016570); Histone modifications (GO:0016570) —DISRUPTS→ Neurogenesis (GO:0022008); Neurogenesis (GO:0022008) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental abnormality (HP:0011344); Neurogenesis (GO:0022008) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Hematopoiesis (GO:0030097) —INCREASES→ Neurogenesis (GO:0022008). Loss-of-function mutations in GATA1 disrupt hematopoiesis, leading to thrombocytopenia and dyserythropoietic anemia. In contrast, mutations in H3-3A in BLBN1 alter histone modifications, disrupting neurogenesis and causing neurodevelopmental abnormalities and intellectual disability. The proposed convergence is on the shared cellular machinery and regulatory networks that govern both hematopoiesis and neurogenesis, such as epigenetic regulation and transcriptional control, which, when dysregulated, can manifest as distinct yet mechanistically linked disease phenotypes.

partners.mechanism_chain: GATA1 (HGNC:4143) —DISRUPTS→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001874); GATA1 (HGNC:4143) —DISRUPTS→ Dyserythropoietic anemia (HP:0001891); ITGA2B (HGNC:6074) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 signaling (GO:0030175); ITGB3 (HGNC:6075) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 signaling (GO:0030175); Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 signaling (GO:0030175) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001874); Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 signaling (GO:0030175) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombasthenia (HP:0001955). Mutations in GATA1 cause X-linked thrombocytopenia with or without dyserythropoietic anemia. Mutations in ITGA2B (encoding the alpha subunit) and ITGB3 (encoding the beta subunit) cause Glanzmann's thrombasthenia. Both GATA1 and the ITGA2B/ITGB3 complex play critical roles in megakaryopoiesis and platelet function. Loss-of-function in GATA1 impacts megakaryocyte development and platelet production, leading to thrombocytopenia and potentially anemia. Loss-of-function in the ITGA2B/ITGB3 complex, a key receptor for fibrinogen, impairs platelet aggregation, leading to thrombasthenia. The convergence is on the downstream consequences of impaired platelet formation and function.

falsification.text: The identification of pathogenic variants in GATA1 in individuals diagnosed with Glanzmann's thrombasthenia would falsify the proposed specific causal gene link, suggesting a broader role for GATA1 in platelet aggregation defects beyond its known impact on platelet production. Conversely, identifying pathogenic variants in ITGA2B or ITGB3 in patients with X-linked thrombocytopenia and dyserythropoietic anemia, without concurrent platelet aggregation defects, would suggest separate mechanistic pathways. Furthermore, the absence of mutations in ITGA2B or ITGB3 in patients with Glanzmann's thrombasthenia would be a falsification.
falsification.gnomad_variant: The presence of common benign variants in ITGA2B or ITGB3 in populations with high prevalence of Glanzmann's thrombasthenia would falsify the pathogenicity of those variants.
